title: POS Sessions
description: Till sessions opened and closed from the Point of Sale.

help.title: About POS sessions
help.overview: A session is one opening of a till, from the opening cash count to the closing count. Sessions are opened and closed on the till. This page only lists them.

sections.title: The states
sections.body: The state is where the drawer is in that opening, not whether the till is allowed to sell.
items: Opening is the count before selling starts.
Opened is the selling window. Cash in and cash out happen here.
Closing is the count at the end. Closed is a finished session.

sections.title: What gets recorded
sections.body: The session is the cash drawer for that opening, plus the sales that were rung on it.
items: Opening balance is what was in the drawer when it opened.
Cash in and cash out are drawer moves with a reason. They are not sales.
Close records the counted cash. Reconcile compares that count with what the session expected from the opening balance, the cash moves, and the cash sales.

sections.title: Who can do it
sections.body: The buttons live on the till. The permission lives on the session.
items: Opening, closing, and reconciling need permission to write the session state.
Cash in and cash out need permission to write cash moves.
The sales from the session are listed under POS orders, filtered by this session.
